H1.note: the chain starts at the C4A copy-number haplotypes; C4B, C1QA and CX3CR1 are listed genes without a claim of their own. The route needs the bridge S5 (C4A to pruning), which no step states

H2.note: the chain starts at the risk alleles (title: CSMD1 loss of function). It ends at a schizophrenia-like phenotype in Csmd1 knockout mice, never at schizophrenia; claim 1 can only reach schizophrenia through H1.4

H3.note: 'CX3CL1-CX3CR1 signalling failure licenses microglia to prune': loss of CX3CR1 raises risk. The chain reaches schizophrenia only from the axis (H3.3), which is not where H3.2 ends

H4.note: 'complement is deficient': reduced C1q raises risk. None of H4's three steps shares a node with the next

H5.note: loss of NXPH3 degrades sensorimotor gating, proposed as a route to schizophrenia; the last link (H5.3) is unsigned

findings.detail: The step H1, H2 and H3 all route through (synapse pruning raises schizophrenia risk) is stated by no cited text; the run's own note says its direction is inferred from the C4A risk direction.
H1.2 ends at 'synapse' (where C4A sits) and H1.3 starts at 'C1q complex'; no step says C4A drives pruning, so the arm needs bridge S5 from texts the run cited (PMID:26814963, 38301948, 42000733).
'C4A binds synapse' is a subcellular localisation (the run's note and UniProt say so), not a binding; curated as RO:0001025 located in.
PMID:22632727 shows pruning depends on microglial CR3/C3; it names neither C1q (H1.3) nor the classical pathway (H2.3). It does state H3.2.
The only text kept for C4A copy number raising C4 protein (PMID:42113976) finds the correlation only in neutrophils and only in patients, so not in plasma, monocytes or controls.

Two of H1's 'contradicting' citations support it: PMID:42000733 reports a positive C4A shift in first-episode psychosis CSF and calls C4A implicated in pruning and risk; PMID:38301948 opens by restating the C4A pruning model.
Confidence 'high', but the C4A-to-pruning link is missing from the chain and no cited text states pruning-to-schizophrenia or C1q-to-pruning.

Supporting citations at no step: tag SNPs rs116633139, rs1150754, rs115035678 (two are for the combined trait 'autism spectrum disorder or schizophrenia', rs116633139 has no named allele); P0C0L5 (C4B, no C4B step); enrichments R-HSA-166663, R-HSA-174577, STRING:GO:0006958; HPA expression records ENSG00000173372, ENSG00000168329.

The mechanism says microglia 'uniquely express C1QA' in brain, but HPA:ENSG00000173372 has C1QA group-enriched with Kupffer cells and macrophages and tissue-enriched in choroid plexus and lymphoid tissue.
No cited text says the CSMD1 risk alleles lower CSMD1; the run's own note admits the direction is assumed, yet H2 is rated 'high'.
'CSMD1 risk alleles / loss of function' merges common GWAS alleles with loss of function, which is exactly what the step should show.
H2.3 ends at synapse elimination, H2.4 starts at the Csmd1 knockout mouse; H2's own chain never reaches schizophrenia and borrows H1.4 to do so.
H2 ends at a 'schizophrenia-like behavioural phenotype' in knockout mice (curated as a mouse refinement of schizophrenia), not at schizophrenia; claim 2 targets that end node.

H2's strongest evidence, genome-wide CSMD1 associations (rs10503253, rs12541020, rs139425113, rs6986895, rs13261217, rs10098869, OT 0.81), is never a step; only rs10503253 sits in the chain, under a step about protein level it cannot state.

Supporting citations at no step: PMID:21926974 (names locus 8p23.2, not CSMD1), rs12541020, rs139425113, rs6986895, rs13261217, rs10098869 (four with no named risk allele), OT:CSMD1-MONDO_0005090, HPA:ENSG00000183117.
H2's only contradicting citation, STRING:C4A-C4B, is a C4A-C4B edge and bears on nothing in H2; the falsification text names the real gap (no experimental STRING edge from CSMD1 to C4A/C4B/C1QA).
The Alliance model annotation calling the Csmd1 knockout a schizophrenia model 'carries no supporting publication'.
H3.2 ends at complement-dependent pruning, H3.3 starts at CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis disruption; H3 reaches schizophrenia only by borrowing H1.4.
H3.1's direction (CX3CR1 restrains microglial activation) rests on unsigned MGI 'abnormal' annotations and an enrichment; the run's note admits the sign is inferred.
OT:CX3CR1-tractability, a supporting citation, quotes UniProt that CX3CR1 'participat[es] in synaptic pruning' (by similarity), while H3's route has CX3CR1 lowering pruning.

Supporting citations at no step: HPA:ENSG00000168329, AGR:MGI:1333815:MP:0000136 (unsigned), STRING:CX3CR1-C1QA (text-mining only), OT:CX3CR1-tractability, R-HSA-9968734 (monocyte differentiation enrichment).
H4.1 has C1q decreasing 'circulating C1q level in psychosis', a molecule lowering itself; the real claim (C1q lower in psychosis) sits in the context field.

The run calls PMID:38301948 a peripheral measure with an unresolved compartment, but it measured CSF C1qA and prefrontal C1QA mRNA (both lower), which already answers part of H4's own falsification test.

PMID:39616737, cited for H4, reports C1QA mRNA increased in high-inflammation schizophrenia and says complement activation may reduce newborn neurons, both against 'deficient complement impairs neurogenesis'.
No H4 step starts where the previous one ends (C1q level; C1q deficiency to abnormal transmission; impaired clearance and neurogenesis to schizophrenia).
H4's only route from C1QA to schizophrenia borrows H1.3 and H1.4 and composes positive, against H4's negative claim: the shared library makes the H1/H4 contradiction explicit.
Neither cited text says impaired clearance or neurogenesis causes schizophrenia; clearance appears in no cited text at all.
Supporting citations at no step: AGR:MGI:88223:MP:0009940, R-HSA-977606 (enrichment), and GWAS:C1QA:no-association, which is also listed as contradicting H1; a null fits neither direction.
H5 cites HPA:ENSG00000183117 for NXPH3 expression ('~4000 nCPM in excitatory and inhibitory cortical neurons'), but that is CSMD1's record (ENSG00000183117 is CSMD1).
The Nxph3 records give increased startle (not gating) and unsigned 'abnormal spatial learning'; nothing shows NXPH3 is required for sensorimotor gating.
Supporting citations at no step: PMID:19455133 (the abstract never names NXPH3), PMID:18923512 (neurexins/neuroligins, no NXPH3), AGR:MGI:1336188:MP:0001392 (abnormal locomotion).
'Sensorimotor gating deficit associated with schizophrenia' has polarity 'unknown' though the label implies one; with no cited text giving it, the link stays unsigned and H5 has no route.
Three steps join two objects or subjects with 'and' (excitatory and inhibitory; clearance and neurogenesis; gating and learning); each was split into two statements.
Made BLN:C4A-highCopyNumber and BLN:CSMD1-schizophreniaRiskAlleles (variant classes with no ID) and BLN:AlphaNeurexins (no class term for the alpha-neurexins; PR has only single isoforms).
PW:0000833 'CX3C chemokine mediated signaling pathway' is in the corpus but render.py has no kind for PW, so the axis was grounded to GO:0016495 (C-X3-C chemokine receptor activity, a function).
'Spatial learning' is only in GO as a synonym of GO:0008542 'visual learning' (rendered label), and NBO:0000175 is not accepted; 'sensorimotor gating' was grounded to GO:0060134 prepulse inhibition.

A 'schizophrenia-like phenotype' in knockout mice has no phenotype term; it was curated as schizophrenia refined to taxon mouse, a disease node, so the chain_ends_at_phenotype claim targets a disease.
The guide's relation table has no row for subcellular localisation; used RO:0001025 located in.
The guide doesn't say if a genotype-dosage correlation (copy number vs protein) for a variant-to-amount effect is 'association_only' or observational evidence; kept as observational.
For unsigned associations whose label implies a direction ('deficit associated with', 'disruption') there's no rule; H3.3 got its sign from the text, H5.3 stayed unsigned.

'Microglial synapse pruning', 'synapse elimination' and 'complement-dependent synapse pruning' merged as GO:0098883, though GO:0150062 has the last as an exact synonym; this merge gives H2 and H3 their only routes to schizophrenia (through H1.4).
'NXPH3-neurexin signalling' merged into NXPH3 (activity is not an entity), as the cited knockout records concern NXPH3 itself.
Immunostaining of human tissue for localisation (PMID:26814963) has no evidence kind; recorded as observational.
The PMID:22632727 abstract never names its species; taxon mouse set from the paper's design (in vivo CR3/C3 disruption), not from the quoted span.
A text against a composed route (CX3CR1 promotes pruning, against H3.1 plus H3.2) has no statement to attach to as refuting, so it is only a finding.
Contradicting citations about gene-disease association (OT scores, null GWAS) fit no step-level statement and had to be excluded under a nearby statement; claims have no evidence slot.
An MGI 'no abnormal phenotype detected' (MP:0002169) for a second allele is a null with no named phenotype; it can't refute a specific phenotype step.
An MGI disease-model annotation with no publication behind it counts as curatedDb, the same as a published phenotype annotation.

A single mouse MGI annotation gives belief 4/5, so S9, S13 and S14 come out 'established' about human CSMD1/C1QA even with taxonConsistent false; the mismatch is flagged but does not discount the statement.
